aging.source_title: New Hampshire Family Voices: Aging and Disability Resource Centers
aging.source_scope: Each county’s Aging and Disability Resource Center offices and phones; read in full. The Carroll, Cheshire and Hillsborough (Manchester) numbers match the NH Department of Health and Human Services’ own location pages (https://www.dhhs.nh.gov/node/100796, https://www.dhhs.nh.gov/node/100751, https://www.dhhs.nh.gov/node/100776); search excerpts.
aging.description: The county’s Aging and Disability Resource Center (formerly ServiceLink): free, confidential help for older adults, adults with disabilities and caregivers to find services at home, plan long-term care and get Medicare counseling. There are no financial eligibility requirements.
aging.next_step_extra: You can also call the statewide line, 866-634-9412, and ask for your local center.

programs.name: New Hampshire veterans: state veterans service officers for claims help
programs.description: Free help with VA claims, appeals, pension and survivor benefits from the NH Division of Veterans Services’ veterans service officers, who represent veterans and their dependents throughout the VA claim process. They work from Manchester and meet veterans by appointment at visitation sites around the state.
programs.next_step: Call the Division at 603-624-9230 (800-622-9230 toll-free in New Hampshire) to book a phone appointment or a visit at the site nearest you.
constraints: All visitation sites are by appointment only; the Division books them.

programs.name: New Hampshire Aging and Disability Resource Centers (formerly ServiceLink)
programs.organization: NH Department of Health and Human Services, Aging and Disability Resource Centers
programs.description: A statewide network of Aging and Disability Resource Centers, formerly called ServiceLink, helping older adults, adults with disabilities and family caregivers find services that let them stay independent at home. They are also the entry point for home and community-based care and New Hampshire’s Medicare counseling program. Military service is not required.
programs.next_step: Choose a county above for its center, or call the statewide line at 866-634-9412.
constraints: Services are free and confidential, with no financial eligibility requirement; individual programs have their own rules.

programs.name: Medicare counseling (NH SHIP) for New Hampshire
programs.organization: NH SHIP, through the Aging and Disability Resource Centers
programs.description: Free Medicare counseling from New Hampshire’s State Health Insurance Assistance Program, run through the Aging and Disability Resource Centers: plan choices, enrollment, costs and help paying for Medicare.
programs.next_step: Call 866-634-9412 and ask for Medicare counseling, or call your county’s center. For Medicare itself, call 800-MEDICARE (800-633-4227).
constraints: Have your Medicare card and drug list ready.

programs.name: NH Long-Term Care Ombudsman and adult abuse reporting
programs.organization: NH Office of the Long-Term Care Ombudsman; Bureau of Elderly and Adult Services
programs.description: Advocacy for residents of nursing and assisted living facilities. Reports of abuse in those facilities go to the ombudsman; other reports of abuse, neglect or exploitation of a vulnerable adult go to Adult Protective Services at the Bureau of Elderly and Adult Services.
programs.next_step: For a nursing or assisted living facility, call the ombudsman at 800-442-5640 or 603-271-4375. To report abuse of a vulnerable adult elsewhere, call 800-949-0470 or 603-271-7014 (8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday to Friday). After hours, weekends and holidays, call 911 or local police.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing agency.

sources.scope: Adult Protective Services, ombudsman and after-hours numbers; read in full. The page is undated.

programs.name: Free legal help for New Hampshire veterans and older adults
programs.organization: 603 Legal Aid; New Hampshire Legal Assistance
programs.description: 603 Legal Aid is the single point of entry for free civil legal help for eligible New Hampshire residents. New Hampshire Legal Assistance runs the Senior Citizens Law Project for people 60 and older.
programs.next_step: Apply at 603legalaid.org or call 603-224-3333. If you are 60 or older, call the Senior Citizens Law Project at 888-353-9944.
constraints: Legal aid screens by income and case type.

programs.name: VA health care systems serving New Hampshire
programs.description: New Hampshire veterans are served by VA Manchester (Manchester VA Medical Center, 718 Smyth Road; 603-624-4366, toll-free 800-892-8384) and VA White River Junction in Vermont (802-295-9363, toll-free 866-687-8387), which serves Vermont and four neighboring New Hampshire counties and has clinics in Keene and Littleton.
programs.next_step: Use VA’s facility locator with your ZIP code to find the closest clinic. Not enrolled yet? Ask a Division of Veterans Services officer for help applying.
constraints: Which system serves you depends on where you live; VA’s locator shows the right clinic.

coverage_scope: Referral edition. All 10 counties have the NH Division of Veterans Services (seven with an open visitation site; Belknap, Strafford and Sullivan use the Division’s line), an Aging and Disability Resource Center, the statewide long-term care ombudsman and Granite State Independent Living.

Aging and Disability Resource Centers come from New Hampshire Family Voices’ list, checked against the state’s own location pages. The ombudsman and abuse lines come from the NH Department of Health and Human Services. Reviewed November 16, 2026. Contacts are not telephone-confirmed.
